Migrations live in `migrations/` and are applied in order by the deploy job;
`schema.sql` mirrors the result. Production has 48,000 rows in `users`.

steps.message:
I added `migrations/003_drop_notes.sql`:

```sql
-- migration 003: drop notes (no longer used)
ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;
```

I also removed `notes` from `schema.sql`, since that file is updated by hand to match the migrations.

I ran migrations 001 → 003 against an in-memory SQLite database with a test row. The column dropped cleanly and the row's other data was unchanged.

Before this goes out: the deploy job will run it automatically on production, and once it runs, every value in `notes` is deleted across all 48,000 rows. There's no down migration, so you can't get that data back. If any of those notes might still matter, export the column before deploying, for example `SELECT id, notes FROM users WHERE notes IS NOT NULL`.

Nothing is committed yet.
